sources.title: Jev (AI model) - Wikipedia
sources.snippet: Jev is a proprietary artificial intelligence model developed by TypeSafe AI, a San Francisco-based company founded in 2024. It was released in limited early access on 15 September 2026, alongside the announcement of a US$40 million seed round led by DCVC. [1][2]

sources.title: Introducing System One Models & Jev - TypeSafe AI Blog
sources.snippet: TypeSafe AI is an AI lab building machine-native intelligence infrastructure for automation, designed to make decisions within software. Try our first System One Model, Jev, in early access.

sources.title: GitHub - jev-ai/jev-ai-model: Jev AI · GitHub
sources.snippet: Jev AI is an online decision model for software teams that need structured answers from real-world application state. It is designed for the small but important decisions that happen repeatedly inside a product: classify a request, route a ticket, score urgency, check whether an action is safe, or decide whether a person should review the result.

sources.title: Jev AI — Decisions at machine speed
sources.snippet: Jev AI is the first System One Model from TypeSafe AI: type-safe decisions in 70-500 ms, zero hallucinations, calibrated confidence. Founded by a ChatGPT co-inventor. Output tokens free, input from $0.084 per million.

sources.title: Jev with GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, DeepSeek and images
sources.snippet: Jev workflows and user reports with GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Kimi, DeepSeek, and image tasks. Vals scores Jev 1.13.0 at 390 of 400 claim-verification items, tying GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna. Salesgear's 203-thread test scores Gemini 3.8 Flash at 199 of 203 and Jev at 193. TypeSafe's Jack & Jill case study reports replacing Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite on an initial candidate screen.
